A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DisentangO and retain matching methods, physical experiments, and theoretical results. Text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original supervised HGO, semi-supervised Mechanical MNIST, and unsupervised heterogeneous-material experiments, including prediction errors, ablations, and latent visualizations.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds baseline evaluations, a UFNO backbone experiment, and synthetic latent-identifiability results in Tables 4–5.

M1.justification: The core task-wise lifting adaptation, VAE, losses, and supervision procedures remain. Appendix B.2 adds DisentangO-UFNO, replacing the IFNO backbone with UFNO while retaining the surrounding framework. This is a limited architectural adaptation.

E1.justification: The HGO, Mechanical MNIST, and two heterogeneous-material scenarios are retained. Appendix C.4 adds a controlled synthetic mapping with known two-dimensional generative factors for identifiability evaluation, a limited extension beyond the existing physical datasets.

E2.justification: Table 1 expands from five to fourteen baselines, adding UFNO, WNO, PIANO, CAMEL, SMDP, InVAErt, FUSE, FUSE-f, and convVAE. PIANO also joins the corresponding comparisons in Tables 2–3, and MetaUFNO appears in the new backbone comparison.

E3.justification: Appendices B.1–B.2 revise the reported first-experiment depth of DisentangO and MetaNO from 16 to 8 layers. The new synthetic protocol varies training tasks over 3, 5, 7, and 9, uses 100 validation and 500 test tasks, and evaluates MCC and R². Per-epoch timing comparisons are also added. These changes do not establish that retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Existing latent-dimension, loss-weight, supervision, and traversal analyses remain. Table 4 newly tests dependence on the operator backbone. Appendix C.4, Table 5, and Figure 12 test how task variability affects recovery of known latent factors and the identifiability rank condition, substantially extending validation of central methodological claims.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The expanded discussion of Gaussian latent distributions concerns the model, rather than a new practice for reporting experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: Original error entries are retained, but numerous results are added. Table 1 adds FUSE's 4.99% inverse error alongside DisentangO's retained 4.63%, reducing the reported nearest-comparator margin from 68.2% to 7.2%. PIANO adds 13.73% and 50.71% errors in Tables 2–3. Tables 4–5 add backbone results and synthetic recovery scores, including MCC increasing from 0.7836 to 0.9121 across 3 to 9 training tasks.

T1.justification: The generative premise changes from the one-to-one relation b=m(z) in v1 Equation 3.5 to b sampled from a distribution and z sampled conditionally on b in v2 Equation 3.4. The observation model also explicitly incorporates discrete noisy measurements. New Appendix A.2 derives the linear-independence condition for conditional exponential-family distributions. The identifiability conclusions and proof arguments are retained, but their formal setup is substantially revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central contributions: joint forward and inverse modeling, disentanglement from neural-operator parameters, component-wise identifiability under sufficient variability, and utility across three supervision settings. Hypernetwork terminology and additional evidence do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: New Appendices B.4–B.5 explain probabilistic encoding, latent visualization, backbone dependence, scalability, and the accuracy–interpretability trade-off. They explicitly delimit applicability to parametric PDE families. The conclusion replaces the earlier limited-number-of-systems caveat with a boundary concerning untested high-dimensional PDEs. These substantially expand the paper's interpretations and limitations.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code/data repository link, extensive architecture and input specifications for the added baselines, fuller documentation of FNO inverse optimization, and per-epoch timings, including its forward/inverse timing breakdown. Appendix C.4 documents the synthetic generator and sampling procedure. These materially expand reproducibility information beyond v1's shorter implementation appendix.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds a substantive hypernetwork discussion, including Ha, Chauhan, Nguyen, Oh and Peng, and Lee, positioning DisentangO relative to weight-generating architectures. It also acknowledges additional physical disentanglement work by Fotiadis, Lingsch, and Tong and adds references supporting the expanded baseline comparisons.

P1.justification: The introduction and related work are extensively condensed and rewritten. Section 3.1 reorganizes the method around explicit notation, a data model, and the operator architecture before the learning objective; assumptions are consolidated and numbered. Supervision scenario numbering is reversed, and the appendices gain several structured explanatory subsections.

P2.justification: Figure 1 gains clearer labels and a detailed caption. The earlier main-text Figures 2–5 are retained but moved after the references and renumbered. Tables are expanded and reformatted, replacing numeric model codes with names and adding a timing column to Table 1. Tables 4–5 and Figure 12 are new, alongside a document-wide conference-format layout change.

improvement.justification: The expanded comparisons address an important weakness in v1 by including much closer inverse competitors, making the performance evidence substantially more informative. The backbone experiment and controlled latent-recovery study test previously unsupported aspects of the method, while implementation details and access information improve reproducibility. Some inconsistencies remain, notably Section 4.3's retained 90.7% advantage despite the added PIANO result implying 89.6%. These limitations do not outweigh the substantial gains in validation and documentation.
